players.product: ZT Systems AI rack/system integration for AMD next-generation accelerated compute (Helios), plus AI rack metal fabrication, liquid-cooling manifolds, busbars and high-layer PCBs

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 (quarter ended March 28, 2026) revenue came in at $4.01 billion, well above the outlook range and up 102% year over year; ZT Systems revenue was $1.88 billion, exceeding expectations because some accelerated compute shipments previously expected in the second half shifted into Q2 on strong execution and customer demand; Core Sanmina revenue grew 7.3%; non-GAAP operating margin 6.4% (third straight quarter at 6% or above) and non-GAAP diluted EPS $3.16 (+125%).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $4.01 billion (+102% YoY); ZT Systems $1.88 billion; Core Sanmina +7.3%; non-GAAP op margin 6.4%; EPS $3.16

quarterly_data.signal: Communication networks, cloud, AI infrastructure end market came in at $2.77 billion, 'almost 280% growth'; Core Sanmina contributed $891 million (up 22% year over year) and ZT Systems $1.88 billion, driven by accelerated compute, general purpose compute and storage plus IP switching/routing, optical systems, pluggables, broadband access and 5G; industrial, energy, medical, defense/aerospace and automotive delivered 31% or $1.24 billion, flat. IMS segment revenue $3.58 billion (+123.5%), CPS $461 million (+12.2%).
quarterly_data.figure: comms/cloud/AI infrastructure $2.77 billion (almost 280% growth); Core Sanmina portion $891 million (+22%); IMS $3.58 billion (+123.5%); CPS $461 million (+12.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 FY2026 outlook: revenue between $3.2 billion and $3.5 billion (Core Sanmina $2.2 billion-$2.3 billion, ZT Systems $1.0 billion-$1.2 billion); ZT revenue is down sequentially because accelerated compute orders shifted from the second half into Q2; non-GAAP operating margin 6.4%-6.9%, non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.55-$2.85, capital expenditures $95 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $3.2 billion to $3.5 billion; ZT Systems $1.0 billion-$1.2 billion; op margin 6.4%-6.9%; capex $95 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2026 outlook: revenue $13.7 billion-$14.3 billion (midpoint $14 billion, growth of approximately 73%), Core Sanmina growing high single digits and ZT Systems 'well within the $5 billion-$6 billion annualized range' communicated at the May acquisition announcement; non-GAAP operating margin 6.3%-6.6%, EPS $10.75-$11.35. Management is 'increasingly confident' in revenue of $16 billion+ in fiscal 2027; CFO framed Core Sanmina near $10 billion next year and ZT contributing '$6 billion-$7 billion', while still assuming the vast majority of ZT business will be consignment.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $13.7 billion-$14.3 billion; ZT $5 billion-$6 billion annualized; op margin 6.3%-6.6%; FY2027 $16 billion+

quarterly_data.signal: ZT Systems integration: the core of the business is integrated and most of the capital investments in incremental power, liquid cooling and test cell capacity are made to be production ready for the next generation of accelerated compute. Sanmina has secured next-generation accelerated compute business with both hyperscale and OEM customers ('multiple hyperscalers and ODMs') and is finalizing customer production schedules; it has started shipping pre-production volumes. The next-generation product is 'scheduled to be out in September' and on track, but the fiscal 2026 opportunity 'isn't really huge' - it is 'more of an FY 2027 play'. ZT is expanding beyond its legacy handful of customers to more hyperscale/CSP customers, OEMs and neoclouds, aims to fill all capacity and would invest more if wins continue; future vertical integration will add subassemblies (fabricated subsystems) from Core Sanmina.

Supply: material shortages 'around the memory, custom ASICs, and things like that' are expected to continue through the rest of the year and potentially into 2027; 'last quarter, we could have shipped a little bit more if we were able to get every part number that we needed.' Book-to-bill was better than 1.1; the Core Sanmina communication networks and cloud infrastructure business has grown 20%+ year over year for the last 6 quarters and 'Could be growing a lot more' with more components and equipment. Component shortages also affected revenue timing and profitability for one CPS product business, expected to be resolved in the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill better than 1.1; Core comms/cloud growth 20%+ YoY for the last 6 quarters

quarterly_data.signal: Networking/optics: 'Yes, we're shipping 1.6 TB switches' (in new product introduction) for multiple switch customers; Sanmina builds optical systems and optical pluggables around 400 and 800 and is 'also developing 1.6 TB in a pluggables', and has been investing in custom optical modules. Data center capabilities also include high-technology PCBs (North America and Singapore), mechanical racks and enclosures, liquid cooling (cooling manifolds, busbars), compute/storage ODM and custom memory.

Industrial and energy: growth driven by power generation and distribution; Sanmina is investing in transformers engineering and design with multiple customers and expects nice growth especially in 2027, and is 'expanding energy business for AI data centers all the way from engineering, design to full system and vertical integration'; semiconductor capital equipment demand is moving up.

Cash and balance sheet: Q2 cash flow from operations $399 million, capital expenditures $57 million (below outlook on timing), free cash flow $342 million; inventory net of customer advances $2.1 billion (up 75% on the ZT acquisition), liquidity approximately $3.7 billion, net leverage 0.56x; repurchased approximately 1.1 million shares for approximately $160 million and the board authorized an additional $600 million of repurchases. Inventory is expected to rebuild, more in Q4, to prepare for the new accelerated compute business.
quarterly_data.figure: CFO $399 million; capex $57 million; FCF $342 million; inventory $2.1 billion; buyback authorization $600 million

connects_to.relationship: ZT Systems builds AMD next-generation accelerated compute (Helios) racks/systems; pre-production validation with AMD and joint hyperscale/OEM customers

contracts.signal: CEO: 'We did not ship any accelerated compute of NVIDIA product. Whatever we shipped, it was all based on AMD technology.' A customer pulled in accelerated compute products originally scheduled for Q3/Q4; the Q2 ZT business was all new-platform accelerated compute, which the CFO described as 'the MI300 series business, kind of the current version of accelerated compute, but new for us'.
